ajtowns:
  • Opcode blacklisting – defeats the purpose: if we’re trying to have big signature data on the regular stack to be able to manipulate it in interesting ways, then this approach would blacklist some of those interesting ways

I mean, you can still do interesting things, e.g. OP_SIZE on SHRINCS sigs would let you restrict signatures to stateful or stateless paths. Just not duplication.

ajtowns:
  • Isolated sig stack – this seems the simplest approach if you’re willing to throw away the idea of scripts doing clever things with signature data (or defer it until GSR/similar is implemented on some separate track). It has the additional potential benefit that an isolated stack could get a greater discount (as discussed here).

I had assumed that new witness discounts would probably not be deployed alongside SHRINCS, but if you’re considering that, then we should probably do something a little more thorough. One possible idea here, similar to @sipa’s witness styles idea

Segwit commitment to post-quantum witness data? Protocol Design
One suggested design, similar to @sipa’s that implements chaining. Format Add a new transaction field, specifically for new transaction data format extensions. Call it the “extensions” field. An “extension” on the wire is just an opaque blob of data followed by an optional hash, encoded as compact_size(len(data)) || data || hash.
